verdict: FAIL: reopen coverage expansion and stopping passes; retain redundant questions only with zero novelty credit.
scope: Complete multiplayer first-printing base Oath: first and later setup, all four Oaths and true Visions, Empire, and Chronicle. Excludes Clockwork Prince and New Foundations.
method: Independent source-first review of every question and expected answer, all Law procedural sections, complete multiplayer Playbook prose and examples, errata, and both reference images. No summary, reader responses, grades, or previous audits read.

findings.finding: Two reported zero-addition passes do not establish saturation. Broad section-level mappings conceal untested procedural branches; ten exact additions are proposed below. This is not a demand for arbitrary numeric variants.
Law 7.6.1 forced Citizenship is mapped to Q019, whose question/key require an ordinary Scepter offer and exactly one Reliquary relic. It does not test becoming a Citizen without an offer.

Law 7.1.2 is mapped to Q027/Q040. Q027 tests the occupied-card battle-plan exception and out-of-turn payment, while Q040 tests component limits. Neither directly tests the ordinary occupied-card payment prohibition or continued access to a costless power on that card.
sources: Card Reference p1, Rules of Use: Exhaustion

findings.finding: Playbook pp29–30 is mapped to Q020–24/Q052, but none tests opening and sorting the Archive Packet before the first Chronicle. First-game setup pp6–7 is represented by Q025 but lacks its distinct discard/deck setup procedure.
sources: Playbook p29 Ending Your First Game

findings.finding: Law 2.11 is mapped to Q001/Q002/Q036, none of whose keys gives the mandatory +1 defense die for Oathkeeper and +2 for Usurper. Q017 mentions sharing the bonus but does not specify either bonus; the errata also classifies it as a Campaign modifier.

Law 4.1.4/Opportunity Site Reference is mapped to Q006. That question asks about the People’s Favor, and its key merely says optional opportunity-site income. It does not test pawn presence, one token total, taking it from the site rather than a bank, or the named eligible sites.

Ledger maps Law 5.2 Muster to Q061, but Q061 is Plains/Mountain Campaign dice; River Muster is Q062. Grouped Law 2.3–5 mapping includes Q068 action sequencing without a relevant relic/banner test. These do not invalidate Q011 or Q062 but reduce mapping reliability.

The introductory turn/round procedure in Law 4 is not explicitly mapped or tested: Chancellor first every round, clockwise one turn each, phases in order, end-round victory check before advancing. Individual phase/action questions do not ask this overall procedure.

The blanket Glossary procedural-verbs mapping does not establish coverage of Kill’s component destination or the distinction between moving/swapping and playing a card. These have consequential resource/trigger outcomes.
sources: Law Glossary Kill, Move, Play, Swap

ambiguous_or_incomplete_keys.issue: The phrase “Draw up to three available” can be read as permission to stop voluntarily, conflicting with Q082’s correct mandatory-count answer.
ambiguous_or_incomplete_keys.exact_correction: Replace “Draw up to three available” with “Draw the prescribed three cards, or all available if the source runs out, except when a world-deck Vision stops the draw or a modifier changes the count.”
sources: Playbook p32 Drawing, Playing, and Discarding Cards

ambiguous_or_incomplete_keys.issue: “Citizen targeted by Chancellor likewise” is less precise than the chosen-defender rule, since Imperial sites are jointly ruled and targets need not define which Citizen is the defender.
ambiguous_or_incomplete_keys.exact_correction: Replace that phrase with “If the Chancellor chooses a Citizen as the defender, that Citizen is not an Imperial player during this Campaign.”

ambiguous_or_incomplete_keys.issue: “Facedown banners inactive” can be mistaken for the separate banner placards; the rule is about restriction banners on facedown cards.
ambiguous_or_incomplete_keys.exact_correction: Replace with “Restriction banners on facedown cards do not apply.”

novelty_review.standard: A later question has zero novelty credit if all of its rule/outcome/timing content is already in the earlier questions/keys, even if it is useful as a targeted regression scenario. Preserve historical IDs rather than deleting or renumbering them.

rejected_new_coverage_candidates.reason: Conditional board/site defense and shield-only doubling are already explicitly specified by Q015; Q014 already lists defense dice from targets.
Q019 already gives recipient choice of shortage removals/replacements; Q034/Q035 already distinguish board conversion from unchanged purple map garrisons.
Q006 explicitly resolves repeat-if-Mob before the final threshold flip; Q012 identifies Recover as the reset to the normal side. The six-favor example adds no rule.
Q002 already requires revealed Vision at Wake and three world Visions; Q010 locates the ordinary reveal in a minor action; Q068 locates normal actions in Act.
Q004’s complete ordered round-eight answer already distinguishes Exile Usurper from mere Oathkeeper and supplies Visionary/Empire fallback.
Q020 already explicitly covers multiple-method Oath choice, newly flipped former Citizens being ineligible, other Exiles, one replacement warband per accepted site, and ignoring the ordinary offer.
Q016 already says take all targeted relics/banners, may banish, may burn half rounded down, and separately applies banner seizure.
Q015 already defines board-force attack-die choice, immediate skull kills and exact sacrifice; Q038 orders skulls before halving; Q040 forbids unprompted extra loss.

Q007 already defines personal-bank refresh, exact Citizen marker and saving/cap. The additional bracket numbers are useful reference/regression data but introduce no independent procedural rule under the ledger’s no-number-variants standard.

The source-required Search draw count belongs in Q008’s base Search answer. Retain Q082 as a disambiguating regression question and correct Q008’s “up to” wording; do not claim a second distinct rule for the same draw-count requirement.

borderline_but_retained_as_novel.reason: Although Q017 mentions side sharing and defender arbitration, Q070 adds the explicit limit that a prohibition on other battle plans applies to the entire side while your site/board remain individual. This is a real errata boundary.

proposed_additions.title: Turn/round sequence and track initialization
proposed_additions.question: At setup, where do the Round and Visions Drawn markers start? Who takes the first turn of every round, in which direction does play proceed, what phases make a turn, and when is an end-of-round victory check made relative to moving the round marker?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Both markers start on their first/star spaces (Round1 and Visions Drawn0). Starting with the Chancellor each round, go clockwise with one turn per player. Each turn is Wake, Act, Rest in that order. After every player has taken a turn, the round ends: check the applicable end-of-round victory condition before advancing the round marker; round8 ends automatically.
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: First-game card/deck preparation differs from later setup
proposed_additions.question: During the first-game packet setup, do players make the later-game bottom-deck adviser draws or shuffle the ordered packet world deck? How are the regional discards and the Reliquary/relic deck prepared?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Use the assigned facedown advisers instead of later-game adviser draws. Put three facedown cards in the Cradle discard, three in the Provinces discard and five in the Hinterland discard. Put the remaining41 denizen/Vision cards on the World Deck space in Packet B order. Give the Chancellor the Grand Scepter, put Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain, put the next four relic cards facedown in the four Reliquary spaces, and the remaining15 on the Relic Deck space. Preserve the packet instructions/order rather than replacing this with later setup’s bottom draws and random preparation.
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: First Chronicle Archive initialization
proposed_additions.question: Before resolving the first game’s Chronicle, how must the unopened Archive Packet be prepared?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Open the Archive Packet. Put the eight cardboard separators in the small box compartment. Put the six edifices in their matching-suit sections. Shuffle each of the six suit stacks separately and put each stack in its matching section; this forms the Archive. Then use the Chronicle aid and Law8 to pack/save the game.
source_references: Playbook p29 Ending Your First Game
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Forced Citizenship bypasses ordinary offer
proposed_additions.question: If a power lets an Exile become a Citizen with no offer, is a Grand Scepter offer or exactly one Reliquary relic still required, and which status-conversion consequences still apply?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. Forced Citizenship follows the power and the acceptance/conversion procedure in6.6.2 without requiring the ordinary offer in6.6.1 or its promised Reliquary relic. Flip the board to Citizen, replace board/map warbands with available purple warbands with the Exile choosing shortage removals/replacements, discard a revealed Vision, flip a held Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if it is their turn, and refresh Supply to the leftmost space. Do not invent an ordinary promised exchange when there was no offer.
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Ordinary card exhaustion and costless use
proposed_additions.question: A normal Action/modifier card already holds favor or a secret. May you place another favor/secret on it to pay for its power? May its power still be used if it has no cost, and what special case changes the payment rule?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Normally you cannot place favor or secrets on a card that already has either, so you cannot pay such a placement cost. Occupancy does not prevent using a power that has no cost. Battle plans specifically allow placing payment on an occupied card, while still being usable only once per Campaign; this does not permit Muster or Trade on an occupied card.
source_references: Card Reference p1 Rules of Use: Exhaustion
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Title defense modifier
proposed_additions.question: What mandatory defense-die bonus does the Oathkeeper title give on its Oathkeeper side versus its Usurper side? Is this a Campaign modifier, and how does Supremacy apply it to Imperial defense?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: The Oathkeeper must add one defense die; the Usurper must add two. The title bonus is a Campaign modifier. For Supremacy the Chancellor holds the title if the Empire meets the goal and always adds its power when any Imperial player defends. Apply the errata’s side-sharing permissions to participating Imperial defenders/Allies in other Oaths as well.
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Move/swap versus play triggers
proposed_additions.question: A power says to move or swap a denizen rather than play it. Must this obey site/adviser capacities and tree/person/locked restrictions? Does the movement by itself award the favor for playing to a site or trigger a When Played power?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Move follows capacity, play-placement and restriction rules (2.8.1,5.1.4,7.2); Swap moves both prompted pieces to each other’s locations and also follows those movement rules. A move/swap is not itself a play, so it does not by itself award the favor for playing to a site or trigger When Played. A power explicitly saying to play follows the Play rules and those triggers.
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Killed-warband component destination
proposed_additions.question: When a Citizen’s purple warband is killed by a skull, sacrifice, or Campaign loss, which bank receives it? How does this differ from moving a defeated force’s surviving warbands?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Kill moves a warband to the personal bank of the player of that color: purple goes to the Chancellor’s personal bank even when killed from a Citizen’s board. Sacrifice means choosing to kill one’s own warband. Defeated survivors move to a board rather than to a personal bank; in Imperial defense surviving site warbands go to the Chancellor’s board and survivors already on Citizen boards stay there.
source_references: Law 5.5.7.I Empire box as relocated by errata
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Bandits excluded from victory competition
proposed_additions.question: Bandits rule more faceup sites than any player. Do they compete for the Oathkeeper or Vision goals or prevent a player from having the most sites among players?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. Bandits act as a neutral defender for Campaign purposes and rule empty faceup sites, but they do not compete for victory goals. Compare the relevant players, not bandits, when resolving those goals.
source_references: Law Glossary Rule as corrected by errata
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

proposed_additions.title: Opportunity-site Wake income
proposed_additions.question: At Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City, when and from where may a player take income? Can they take both one favor and one secret, use a remotely ruled site, or take from a bank if that site is empty?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: At the end of Wake, after the People’s Favor procedure, Exile win check and title flip, a player whose pawn is at the eligible site may take one favor or one secret from that site. It is one token total, not one of each; remote rule alone does not qualify, and an empty site supplies nothing rather than a substitute token from a bank.
proposed_additions.novelty: An untested core procedure or consequential exception; see finding/coverage notes.
proposed_additions.recommended_disposition: Append afterQ082 with stable new ID after adjudication; do not renumber historical questions.

coverage_assessment.reason: Broad mapped ranges are not equivalent to question/key coverage of every passage. Reopen expansion, append source-backed gaps, and rerun two fresh source sweeps after adjudication. Repeated coverage may remain as regression entries with zero novelty credit.
coverage_assessment.remaining_scope_notes: Ordinary card-specific power databases are not part of the assigned sources; no rules for such unprovided cards were invented. Printed examples illustrate core rules. Group Agreements p31 describes optional group choices, not mandatory new game rules. Clockwork Prince material and New Foundations remain excluded.

passage_audit_notes.Law1: Q021–24 cover ordinary later setup resources, sites, board inheritance and card draws. Missing marker initialization and first-time exception/deck handling addressed byA01/A02. Chancellor selection by any method and random seating are setup choices, not new tactical outcome branches; include exact setup text if summary claims a full setup recipe.

passage_audit_notes.Law3: All four Oaths/Visions, strict Vision ties, successor conditions and ordered victory routes are covered; late duplicates do not create additional coverage.
passage_audit_notes.Law4: Wake/Rest/action sequencing individually covered. Overall round order and actual Opportunity income requireA01/A10.
passage_audit_notes.Law5: Search/Muster/Trade/Recover/Campaign/Travel substantive procedures covered, subject toQ008 wording correction and killed-warband destinationA08.
passage_audit_notes.Law6: Ordinary minor actions, Citizenship offer/conversion and both exile routes covered.
passage_audit_notes.Law7: Most power rules covered; ordinary exhaustion/costless exception and forced Citizenship needA05/A04. Title modifier needsA06.
passage_audit_notes.Law8: Chronicle substantive later-game procedures covered, including errata and Archive healing. First-time Archive preparation missingA03.
passage_audit_notes.Law9: Interpretation, component limits, information, unprompted losses and binding promises covered.
passage_audit_notes.Law10: Most operational glossary meanings covered by action questions, but generic Move/Swap versusPlay andKill destinations requireA07/A08. Bandits not competing needsA09.

Optional group-agreement examples are guidance and do not justify inventing mandatory undo/error-handling rules.
